festival.name: Futurika Fest
festival.subtitle: AI & Creative Tech Summit
festival.location: DOX Centre for Contemporary Art & DOX+ Hall, Prague, Czech Republic
festival.type: International festival and tech summit of generative AI, creative coding, digital media arts and open-source software engineering
festival.summary: A three-day festival in Prague that brings together generative AI researchers, creative technologists, open-source engineers and media artists for keynotes, workshops and live performances.

stage.name: Prompt & Vision Hall
stage.type: Keynotes, Generative Art, Media Performances & AI Demos

stage.name: Tech & Code Lab
stage.type: Technical Talks, LLM Architecture, Agentic Workflows & Live Coding

performer.name: Dr. Elena Rostova
performer.headline_topic: Cognitive Aesthetics & Neural Style Transfer in Modern Cinema
performer.bio: Elena Rostova spent a decade restoring archive film before moving into machine vision, and now leads the creative AI team at Synthetix. Her studio work tests how far style transfer can go before audiences stop trusting what they see on screen.

performer.name: Marcus Vance
performer.headline_topic: From Diffusion to Reality: The Evolution of Text-to-3D Synthesis
performer.bio: Marcus Vance founded HoloMesh Labs after years as a technical artist in games. The company builds tools that turn rough text briefs into editable 3D assets for small production studios.

performer.name: Aoi Tanaka
performer.headline_topic: Generative Audiovisual Symphony: Real-Time Latent Space Soundscapes
performer.bio: Aoi Tanaka composes for concert halls and galleries using instruments trained on field recordings from Japanese coastal towns. Their pieces change each night in response to the room and the audience.

performer.name: Liam Hartley
performer.role: Research Fellow at the Institute for Synthetic Media Ethics
performer.headline_topic: Ethics of Synthetic Media: Deepfakes, Watermarking, and Ownership
performer.bio: Liam Hartley studies how synthetic media affects evidence, journalism and consent. As a research fellow at the Institute for Synthetic Media Ethics, he advises newsrooms on provenance and labelling standards.

performer.name: Sofia Benitez
performer.headline_topic: Autonomous Avatars: The Psychology of Synthetic Brand Influencers
performer.bio: Sofia Benitez has directed campaigns for fashion and consumer brands for fifteen years. At PixelSphere she now researches why audiences form attachments to virtual characters they know are not real.

performer.name: Jan Novák
performer.role: NLP Director at Vltava AI Hub
performer.headline_topic: Czech Language Models: Preserving Cultural Heritage through Open Weights
performer.bio: Jan Novák directs natural language research at the Vltava AI Hub, a Prague lab focused on smaller European languages. He coordinates a volunteer effort to digitise Czech archives as open training data.

performer.name: Chloe Dubois
performer.headline_topic: AI-Augmented Architecture: Algorithmic Urbanism and Future Habitats
performer.bio: Chloe Dubois is a principal architect at Studio Biomimic, where generative models feed into real planning decisions. Her housing projects in Lyon and Marseille use simulation to reduce summer heat in dense neighbourhoods.

performer.name: Tariq Al-Mansoor
performer.headline_topic: Generative Typography and Dynamic Branding Systems
performer.bio: Tariq Al-Mansoor designs identity systems at BrandSynth that behave like software rather than static logos. He trained as a type designer working in Arabic and Latin scripts, and multi-script support shapes his tools.

performer.name: Dr. Miriam Kováčová
performer.role: Senior Lecturer at Prague School of Digital Arts
performer.headline_topic: Bio-Digital Art: Cellular Automata Meets Neural Networks
performer.bio: Miriam Kováčová teaches at the Prague School of Digital Arts and runs a small wet lab for artists. Her installations let living cell cultures and neural networks influence one another's growth.

performer.name: Arjun Patel
performer.role: VP of XR Research at NeuraVision
performer.headline_topic: Interactive Spatial Computing with Real-time Diffusion Engines
performer.bio: Arjun Patel leads extended reality research at NeuraVision, working on headsets that generate scenes as the wearer moves. He previously built real-time rendering engines for flight simulators.

performer.name: Greta Lindholm
performer.role: Lead Game Designer at Nordic Worlds
performer.headline_topic: AI in Game Design: Generating Living Worlds without Static Assets
performer.bio: Greta Lindholm leads game design at Nordic Worlds, an independent studio known for open-world survival titles. She focuses on systems where quests and characters emerge from play instead of being scripted.

performer.name: Lucas Rossi
performer.headline_topic: Cinematography Reimagined: Virtual Production with Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF)
performer.bio: Lucas Rossi has supervised visual effects on European features and streaming series at CineTech Milan. His crews were among the first in Italy to replace location reshoots with captured neural scenes.

performer.name: Zhenya Morozov
performer.headline_topic: Post-Photography: Authenticity in the Age of Midjourney v8
performer.bio: Zhenya Morozov curates FutureLens Gallery, which shows photography and image synthesis side by side. Their exhibitions ask visitors to guess how each picture was made and record what changes their mind.

performer.name: Amara Okafor
performer.role: AI Inclusion Lead at AfroTech Futures
performer.headline_topic: African Languages in Generative AI: Breaking Linguistic Monoculture
performer.bio: Amara Okafor leads inclusion work at AfroTech Futures, supporting speech and text datasets for African languages. She began as a linguist documenting Igbo dialects and still works closely with local speakers.

performer.name: Sven Erikson
performer.headline_topic: Autonomous Robotic Sculpting using Spatial Transformers
performer.bio: Sven Erikson builds sculpting robots at Stockholm Makers, a shared workshop for artists and engineers. His machines carve wood and clay from spoken descriptions and leave the marks of their mistakes visible.

performer.name: Maya Lin-Schumacher
performer.headline_topic: Generative Fashion: Algorithmic Couture and Zero-Waste Patterns
performer.bio: Maya Lin-Schumacher trained as a pattern cutter before moving into computational design at BioWeave. She develops garment patterns that use every centimetre of fabric and works with small European mills.

performer.name: David Miller
performer.headline_topic: Music Without Musicians? Co-Creation Workflows with Generative Audio
performer.bio: David Miller is an independent producer and audio engineer with credits across electronic and film music. He runs open studio sessions where session players and generative tools record together.

performer.name: Dr. Katerina Krausová
performer.headline_topic: Neuroethics of Brain-Computer Interfaces in Digital Arts
performer.bio: Katerina Krausová is a neuroscientist at BrainTech Prague who studies attention and motor imagery. She also consults for artists using brain-computer interfaces and writes on consent in neural data collection.

performer.name: Felix Brandstätter
performer.headline_topic: Real-Time AI Holography: Projecting Volumetric Synthetic Humans
performer.bio: Felix Brandstätter is chief technology officer at HoloStage Vienna, which builds volumetric displays for theatre and live events. He started out as a lighting technician at the Vienna opera houses.

performer.name: Nadia Chernova
performer.role: Philosopher of Technology at Paris Centre for Philosophy of Technology
performer.headline_topic: The Synthetic Muse: Can Neural Networks Possess Intention?
performer.bio: Nadia Chernova is a philosopher of technology at the Paris Centre for Philosophy of Technology. Her writing on authorship and intention has been widely discussed among artists who work with machine learning.

performer.name: Carlos Mendez
performer.headline_topic: Live Latent VJing: Real-time Audio-Reactive Video Synthesis
performer.bio: Carlos Mendez performs as a visual jockey at festivals across Europe and Latin America. He writes his own audio-reactive software and releases most of it under open-source licences.

performer.name: Hanna Weber
performer.role: Story Lead at European Animation Guild
performer.headline_topic: Generative Storyboarding and Automated Animatic Generation
performer.bio: Hanna Weber leads story development for the European Animation Guild and has boarded three animated features. She mentors small studios on using automation for early drafts without losing a director's voice.

performer.name: Dr. Alexei Voronov
performer.headline_topic: Multi-Agent Simulation of Fictional Societies for Worldbuilding
performer.bio: Alexei Voronov is a complexity scientist at DataMind who models how norms spread through populations. Lately he has applied the same methods to help novelists and game writers test their fictional societies.

performer.name: Zuzana Černá
performer.role: UX Director at Prague Design Collective
performer.headline_topic: Accessible AI UI: Designing Inclusive Prompts for Impaired Creators
performer.bio: Zuzana Černá is UX director at the Prague Design Collective and a long-time accessibility advocate. She co-designs interfaces with blind and low-vision creators and audits AI tools for inclusive interaction.

performer.name: Oskar Blomqvist
performer.headline_topic: Synthetic Botany: Algorithmic Flora Simulation for Interactive Exhibits
performer.bio: Oskar Blomqvist calls himself a digital horticulturist. At Nordic Green he grows simulated gardens for museums and botanic centres, with species modelled on real growth and pollination data.

performer.name: Evelyn Reed
performer.headline_topic: Human-in-the-Loop Filmmaking: Directing Agentic Casts
performer.bio: Evelyn Reed is an independent film director whose last two features combined human actors with AI-driven background characters. She teaches directing workshops on running a set where some of the cast are software.

performer.name: Kenji Takahashi
performer.headline_topic: Hyper-Personalized Interactive Narrative Design
performer.bio: Kenji Takahashi writes interactive fiction at Tokyo StoryLab, where a story's plot adapts to each reader. He has published in print as well, and argues that good branching still needs a strong authorial hand.

performer.name: Alina Popescu
performer.headline_topic: Digital Fashion in the Age of Autonomous Avatars
performer.bio: Alina Popescu is a digital stylist at DigiCouture, dressing virtual characters for games, music videos and brand worlds. She trained in couture in Bucharest and Antwerp before moving to digital-only garments.

performer.name: Matěj Dvořák
performer.headline_topic: The Economics of Generative IP: Licensing Neural Checkpoints
performer.bio: Matěj Dvořák is an intellectual property attorney advising studios and model developers across Central Europe. He helps creators draft licences for training data and fine-tuned model checkpoints.

performer.name: Dr. Rachel Weiss
performer.role: Choreographer & Roboticist at Zurich Arts Lab
performer.headline_topic: Embodied AI in Performance Art: Human-Robot Dance Duets
performer.bio: Rachel Weiss is a choreographer and roboticist at the Zurich Arts Lab. Her duets pair trained dancers with robotic arms that learn phrasing through rehearsal rather than fixed programming.

performer.name: Dr. Alexander Wright
performer.headline_topic: Autonomous Agent Swarms: Multi-Agent Collaboration in Production
performer.bio: Alexander Wright is chief AI scientist at SwarmNet, which runs fleets of cooperating agents for logistics customers. His research focuses on how agents coordinate, fail and recover under real workloads.

performer.name: Petra Horáková
performer.headline_topic: Local LLMs on Edge Hardware: Optimizing 7B Models for MacBook Air
performer.bio: Petra Horáková is a systems engineer at Prague Embedded, where she squeezes language models onto consumer hardware. She maintains a popular set of benchmarks for on-device inference.

performer.name: Dmitri Volkov
performer.headline_topic: Building Deterministic Workflows on Top of Non-Deterministic LLMs
performer.bio: Dmitri Volkov is lead architect at Agentic Stack and has spent years making probabilistic systems dependable enough for regulated industries. He is a strong advocate of typed interfaces between models and code.

performer.name: Sarah Jenkins
performer.headline_topic: Vector Databases at Scale: HNSW Indexing Benchmarks for 100M Records
performer.bio: Sarah Jenkins is a data engineer at PineScale, where she runs vector search clusters holding hundreds of millions of embeddings. She publishes reproducible benchmarks and shares her failures as openly as her results.

performer.name: Tomasz Zielinski
performer.headline_topic: Fine-Tuning Open Source LLMs for Legal & Financial Reasoning
performer.bio: Tomasz Zielinski is a machine learning engineer at Warsaw FinTech. He adapts open language models for legal and financial reasoning, where a wrong answer has a measurable cost.

performer.name: Dr. Hélène Martin
performer.role: Research Scientist at Lyon Institute for AI Research
performer.headline_topic: Mechanistic Interpretability: Peeking Inside Transformer Attention Heads
performer.bio: Hélène Martin is a research scientist at the Lyon Institute for AI Research. She works on mechanistic interpretability, tracing how individual attention heads contribute to a model's behaviour.

performer.name: Martin Svoboda
performer.headline_topic: RAG That Doesn't Hallucinate: Graph Neural Networks meet Dense Retrieval
performer.bio: Martin Svoboda heads AI at SearchBridge, a Brno company building retrieval systems for technical documentation. He joined from enterprise search and remains sceptical of any demo without an evaluation set.

performer.name: Ing. Jakub Kučera
performer.role: Senior Backend Architect at CloudStack Prague
performer.headline_topic: Deploying FastAPI Backend Microservices with Model Quantization
performer.bio: Jakub Kučera is a senior backend architect at CloudStack Prague. He designs Python services that keep quantised models fast and affordable, and mentors junior engineers through the local meetup scene.

performer.name: Olga Ivanova
performer.headline_topic: Synthetic Data Generation for Training Robust Fraud Detection Models
performer.bio: Olga Ivanova is principal data scientist at FinShield, where her team models card and payment fraud. She pioneered the company's use of synthetic transactions to protect customer privacy during training.

performer.name: Lukas Brandt
performer.headline_topic: Rust for Machine Learning: Blazing Fast Tokenizers and Inference Engines
performer.bio: Lukas Brandt is a core contributor to Ferrite ML, an open-source machine learning framework written in Rust. He cares about memory safety, small binaries and removing Python from the serving path.

performer.name: Fatima Zahra
performer.headline_topic: Evaluation Frameworks for LLMs: Automated Benchmarking Beyond MMLU
performer.bio: Fatima Zahra is a quality engineer at EvalHub who builds automated test suites for language models. She argues that teams should treat evaluation like continuous integration rather than a one-off benchmark.

performer.name: Julian Richter
performer.headline_topic: Small Language Models (SLMs) vs. Mega-Models: Efficiency Tradeoffs
performer.bio: Julian Richter is research lead at EfficientAI Munich, where he measures what small models can do per watt. His team helps manufacturers decide when a large cloud model is not worth the cost.

performer.name: Eliška Procházková
performer.headline_topic: Self-Healing Distributed Systems Powered by Observability Agents
performer.bio: Eliška Procházková is a DevOps architect at CloudPeak, running distributed platforms for European retailers. Her current work gives observability agents limited permission to diagnose and repair incidents.

performer.name: Arthur Pendelton
performer.headline_topic: Federated Learning: Collaborative Model Training Without Data Sharing
performer.bio: Arthur Pendelton is a privacy architect at OpenSecure and previously worked with hospitals on shared research data. He designs federated training systems that satisfy both engineers and data protection officers.

performer.name: Maximilian Gruber
performer.headline_topic: Memory Management and KV-Cache Compression in LLM Serving
performer.bio: Maximilian Gruber is an inference engineer at TensorServe who works on the low-level mechanics of model serving. He is best known for practical write-ups on GPU memory and request scheduling.

performer.name: Dr. Veronika Křížová
performer.role: Statistician at Prague Data Science Lab
performer.headline_topic: Causal Inference in Machine Learning: Moving Beyond Correlation
performer.bio: Veronika Křížová is a statistician at the Prague Data Science Lab. She teaches engineers to separate causes from correlations and has worked on studies in public health and online experimentation.

performer.name: Hiroshi Sato
performer.headline_topic: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) Deep-Dive: Adapting Foundation Models
performer.bio: Hiroshi Sato is a machine learning researcher at Kyoto Systems, focusing on fine-tuning methods for constrained budgets. He shares training recipes that let small teams adapt large foundation models.

performer.name: Klára Veselá
performer.headline_topic: Building Real-Time Multimodal Pipelines with WebSockets and WebRTC
performer.bio: Klára Veselá is a full-stack machine learning engineer at StreamVoice, building voice assistants that respond while the user is still speaking. Her work spans browser audio, transport protocols and model serving.

performer.name: Brian O'Connor
performer.headline_topic: Defending Against Prompt Injections and Jailbreaks in Enterprise Agents
performer.bio: Brian O'Connor is a cybersecurity analyst at SecurePrompt who runs red-team exercises against enterprise AI assistants. He came to AI security from penetration testing in the banking sector.

performer.name: Simon Dufresne
performer.headline_topic: Model Distillation: Compressing Frontier Models into Tiny Weights
performer.bio: Simon Dufresne leads AI optimisation at CompresSys, helping companies shrink large models for production. He previously researched knowledge distillation and now focuses on what is lost in compression.

performer.name: Dr. Ondřej Malý
performer.headline_topic: Graph RAG: Connecting Unstructured Knowledge with Neo4j
performer.bio: Ondřej Malý is a knowledge engineer at BioGraph, connecting scientific literature into searchable graphs. He holds a doctorate in computational biology and builds retrieval systems for drug discovery teams.

performer.name: Valerie Dupont
performer.headline_topic: Continuous Alignment: DPO vs RLHF in Continuous Production Cycles
performer.bio: Valerie Dupont is an alignment researcher at Paris AI. She studies how to keep model behaviour stable when training never really stops and user feedback arrives continuously.

performer.name: Tibor Varga
performer.headline_topic: Serverless GPU Orchestration: Cold Start Reduction Strategies
performer.bio: Tibor Varga leads cloud infrastructure at ScalerEU, running GPU capacity across European data centres. He focuses on keeping idle costs low without making users wait for a model to load.

performer.name: Nikola Stanković
performer.headline_topic: Neuromorphic Computing: Spiking Neural Networks in Low-Power IoT
performer.bio: Nikola Stanković is a hardware engineer at NeuroChip, working on spiking neural processors for battery-powered sensors. He designed his first low-power boards for agricultural monitoring.

performer.name: Barbora Němcová
performer.headline_topic: Synthetic Code Generation: Benchmarking Copilots across Python and Rust
performer.bio: Barbora Němcová is a developer advocate at DevStack who tests AI coding tools on real repositories. Her independent comparisons are widely read by engineering teams deciding what to adopt.

performer.name: Goran Petrovic
performer.headline_topic: Time-Series Forecasting with Hybrid Transformer-Mamba Architectures
performer.bio: Goran Petrovic is a quantitative analyst at AlphaStream, modelling energy and commodity markets. He evaluates new sequence architectures by how they perform on noisy live data rather than on clean test sets.

performer.name: Zdeněk Pokorný
performer.headline_topic: Data Lineage and Model Governance under the EU AI Act
performer.bio: Zdeněk Pokorný is a compliance officer at EuroTech Ethics who helps European companies prepare for the EU AI Act. A former software auditor, he translates legal duties into concrete engineering checks.

performer.name: Diana Vance
performer.headline_topic: Semantic Caching for High-Throughput LLM APIs
performer.bio: Diana Vance is backend lead at SwiftServe Cloud, running high-traffic API platforms in Python. She specialises in reducing inference bills through caching and smarter request routing.

performer.name: Emir Kurt
performer.headline_topic: Autonomous Database Query Optimization using Deep Reinforcement Learning
performer.bio: Emir Kurt is a database architect at QueryMind, where he applies reinforcement learning to query planning. He spent ten years tuning production databases by hand and wants to automate the tedious parts.

performer.name: Dr. Laura Fontana
performer.role: Quantum Computing Fellow at Geneva Quantum Lab
performer.headline_topic: Quantum Machine Learning: Exploring Variational Quantum Classifiers
performer.bio: Laura Fontana is a quantum computing fellow at the Geneva Quantum Lab. She investigates where variational quantum methods might help machine learning, and is candid about where they do not.

item.title: Cognitive Aesthetics & Neural Style Transfer in Modern Cinema
item.description: Style transfer can now restyle a whole feature film, but viewers notice more than engineers expect. Elena Rostova opens the festival with audience research and restored archive footage, showing what makes a machine-altered image feel right or wrong.

item.title: From Diffusion to Reality: The Evolution of Text-to-3D Synthesis
item.description: Text-to-3D has moved from blurry experiments to assets that can ship in a real project. Marcus Vance traces that progress and shows which steps of a production pipeline still need an artist.

item.title: Generative Audiovisual Symphony: Real-Time Latent Space Soundscapes
item.description: A live concert in which Aoi Tanaka steers trained sound models through latent space in real time. The piece is built from coastal field recordings and reacts to the acoustics of the hall.

item.title: Ethics of Synthetic Media: Deepfakes, Watermarking, and Ownership
item.description: Who owns a synthetic likeness, and can a watermark survive contact with the internet? Liam Hartley compares current provenance methods and explains where they protect people and where they fail.

item.title: Autonomous Avatars: The Psychology of Synthetic Brand Influencers
item.description: People follow virtual influencers even when they know the character is software. Sofia Benitez presents audience studies on trust and attachment, and sets out what brands should not do with them.

item.title: Czech Language Models: Preserving Cultural Heritage through Open Weights
item.description: Most large models treat Czech as an afterthought. Jan Novák explains how open weights and community-built datasets can keep smaller languages and their cultural memory alive in AI systems.

item.title: AI-Augmented Architecture: Algorithmic Urbanism and Future Habitats
item.description: Chloe Dubois walks through housing projects in which generative models informed real planning decisions. The talk compares algorithmic options with what residents and regulators actually accepted.

item.title: Generative Typography and Dynamic Branding Systems
item.description: A live demonstration of a brand identity that behaves like software. Tariq Al-Mansoor generates type and layouts across Arabic and Latin scripts, then shows how designers keep control of the system.

item.title: Bio-Digital Art: Cellular Automata Meets Neural Networks
item.description: Miriam Kováčová demonstrates an installation in which cellular automata and a neural network shape each other's growth. She also explains what living cultures add that a pure simulation cannot.

item.title: Interactive Spatial Computing with Real-time Diffusion Engines
item.description: Arjun Patel closes the first day on the main stage with a headset demo that generates its surroundings as the wearer moves. He breaks down the latency budget that keeps the experience comfortable.

item.title: Autonomous Agent Swarms: Multi-Agent Collaboration in Production
item.description: Agent demos are easy, but running hundreds of agents in production is not. Alexander Wright opens the Tech & Code Lab with lessons from live logistics deployments, including coordination failures and the recovery patterns that worked.

item.title: Local LLMs on Edge Hardware: Optimizing 7B Models for MacBook Air
item.prerequisites: Laptop with Python 3.11 or newer; at least 16 GB of RAM recommended
item.description: Bring your laptop and run a 7B model locally by the end of the session. Petra Horáková guides you through quantisation choices, memory limits and realistic performance on consumer hardware such as a MacBook Air.

item.title: Building Deterministic Workflows on Top of Non-Deterministic LLMs
item.description: Dependable software needs predictable behaviour, yet language models are probabilistic. Dmitri Volkov shows how typed interfaces, validation layers and retries turn uncertain outputs into workflows that regulated teams can trust.

item.title: Vector Databases at Scale: HNSW Indexing Benchmarks for 100M Records
item.description: How does HNSW indexing behave at 100 million records? Sarah Jenkins shares reproducible benchmarks on recall, latency and memory, including the configurations that looked good and then collapsed.

item.title: Fine-Tuning Open Source LLMs for Legal & Financial Reasoning
item.prerequisites: Python and PyTorch experience; a laptop with access to a cloud GPU notebook
item.description: Fine-tune an open model on a small legal and financial reasoning dataset. Tomasz Zielinski covers data preparation and evaluation, and shows how to tell real improvement from memorised answers.

item.title: Mechanistic Interpretability: Peeking Inside Transformer Attention Heads
item.description: What does a single attention head actually do? Hélène Martin introduces the methods of mechanistic interpretability and uses worked examples to show how researchers trace model behaviour to specific components.

item.title: RAG That Doesn't Hallucinate: Graph Neural Networks meet Dense Retrieval
item.description: Dense retrieval alone often returns plausible but wrong context. Martin Svoboda explains how combining it with graph neural networks reduced hallucinations in a technical documentation assistant, with the evaluation data to prove it.

item.title: Deploying FastAPI Backend Microservices with Model Quantization
item.prerequisites: Familiarity with Python web services; Docker basics helpful
item.description: Jakub Kučera builds and deploys a FastAPI inference service live on stage. Watch a quantised model go from notebook to monitored microservice, including the mistakes that real deployments produce.

item.title: Synthetic Data Generation for Training Robust Fraud Detection Models
item.description: Real fraud data is scarce and sensitive. Olga Ivanova explains how FinShield generates synthetic transactions for training, how the team measures their quality, and where synthetic data misled the models.

item.title: Rust for Machine Learning: Blazing Fast Tokenizers and Inference Engines
item.prerequisites: Working knowledge of Rust or another systems language
item.description: Lukas Brandt writes a fast tokenizer and a small inference engine in Rust in front of the audience. The session ends with a side-by-side performance comparison against a typical Python serving stack.

item.title: AI in Game Design: Generating Living Worlds without Static Assets
item.description: What happens when a game world is generated while you play it? Greta Lindholm opens the second day with lessons from a studio replacing static assets with systems, and explains why designers matter more than ever.

item.title: Cinematography Reimagined: Virtual Production with Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF)
item.description: Neural Radiance Fields have changed how crews capture locations. Lucas Rossi shares footage and budgets from European productions that used virtual production, and explains how the role of the cinematographer is changing.

item.title: Post-Photography: Authenticity in the Age of Midjourney v8
item.description: If an image can be generated in seconds, what still makes a photograph a record? Zhenya Morozov draws on gallery experiments in which visitors judged authenticity, often to their own surprise.

item.title: African Languages in Generative AI: Breaking Linguistic Monoculture
item.description: More than two thousand languages are spoken in Africa, yet few work well in generative AI. Amara Okafor shows how communities are building their own datasets and why ownership of that data matters.

item.title: Autonomous Robotic Sculpting using Spatial Transformers
item.description: A robot arm carves material on stage from a spoken description. Sven Erikson explains the spatial transformer models behind it and why he keeps the machine's errors in the finished work.

item.title: Generative Fashion: Algorithmic Couture and Zero-Waste Patterns
item.description: The fashion industry wastes a large share of its fabric at the cutting stage. Maya Lin-Schumacher shows generated patterns that use the whole cloth, and looks at how small mills can adopt them.

item.title: Music Without Musicians? Co-Creation Workflows with Generative Audio
item.description: Are musicians still needed? David Miller answers with a live co-creation session in which a guitarist, a cellist and generative audio tools build a track in front of the audience.

item.title: Neuroethics of Brain-Computer Interfaces in Digital Arts
item.description: Brain-computer interfaces are entering galleries faster than the rules around them. Katerina Krausová explains what these devices really measure, and which questions of consent artists should ask before using neural data.

item.title: Real-Time AI Holography: Projecting Volumetric Synthetic Humans
item.description: Felix Brandstätter projects a volumetric synthetic performer live in the hall. He explains the display technology and rendering pipeline, and addresses when a digital human stops being comfortable to watch.

item.title: The Synthetic Muse: Can Neural Networks Possess Intention?
item.description: Can a system without desires be said to intend anything? Nadia Chernova ends the day's main-stage programme with a clear philosophical argument about authorship, aimed at artists and sceptics alike.

item.title: Evaluation Frameworks for LLMs: Automated Benchmarking Beyond MMLU
item.prerequisites: Basic Python; a laptop with a code editor
item.description: Single benchmark scores rarely predict how a model behaves in your product. Fatima Zahra helps you build a small automated evaluation suite that runs like continuous integration for prompts and models.

item.title: Small Language Models (SLMs) vs. Mega-Models: Efficiency Tradeoffs
item.description: When does a small model beat a giant one? Julian Richter compares cost, energy and accuracy across real workloads and offers a practical framework for choosing the right size.

item.title: Self-Healing Distributed Systems Powered by Observability Agents
item.description: Eliška Procházková shows what happens when observability agents get limited permission to act. The talk covers the guardrails, approval steps and rollback rules behind automatic incident repair in a production platform.

item.title: Federated Learning: Collaborative Model Training Without Data Sharing
item.description: Hospitals and banks often cannot share raw data, yet they still want better models. Arthur Pendelton explains how federated learning works and where privacy guarantees remain weaker than they sound.

item.title: Memory Management and KV-Cache Compression in LLM Serving
item.description: KV-cache memory is often the true limit on LLM serving. Maximilian Gruber looks inside the serving stack and compares compression and eviction techniques that increase throughput on the same hardware.

item.title: Causal Inference in Machine Learning: Moving Beyond Correlation
item.description: Prediction is not explanation. Veronika Křížová introduces causal inference through worked examples, showing engineers how to avoid confident conclusions drawn from misleading correlations.

item.title: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) Deep-Dive: Adapting Foundation Models
item.prerequisites: Python and PyTorch experience; a laptop with access to a cloud GPU notebook
item.description: Train your own LoRA adapter with Hiroshi Sato. The workshop explains the mathematics in plain terms and then covers rank selection, small datasets and the most common training failures.

item.title: Building Real-Time Multimodal Pipelines with WebSockets and WebRTC
item.prerequisites: Experience with web development; basic understanding of asynchronous code
item.description: Klára Veselá assembles a voice and video assistant live using WebSockets and WebRTC. She shows how to measure every stage of the pipeline and keep the conversation feeling natural.

item.title: Defending Against Prompt Injections and Jailbreaks in Enterprise Agents
item.prerequisites: Laptop with a modern browser; no security background required
item.description: Attack a deliberately vulnerable company assistant, then fix it. Brian O'Connor runs a guided red-team exercise covering prompt injection, jailbreaks and practical defensive layers for enterprise agents.

item.title: Model Distillation: Compressing Frontier Models into Tiny Weights
item.description: Can a tiny model keep most of a frontier model's abilities? Simon Dufresne explains knowledge distillation, shows what is lost during compression, and presents methods to measure the damage.

item.title: Live Latent VJing: Real-time Audio-Reactive Video Synthesis
item.description: Start the final day with a live audiovisual set. Carlos Mendez generates video in real time from the music, then opens up his software to show how the performance works.

item.title: Generative Storyboarding and Automated Animatic Generation
item.description: Storyboards and animatics can now be drafted in hours instead of weeks. Hanna Weber shows how animation teams use that speed for more ideas without giving up the director's voice.

item.title: Multi-Agent Simulation of Fictional Societies for Worldbuilding
item.description: What would your fictional society do during a famine or an election? Alexei Voronov shows how multi-agent simulations help writers and game designers test the logic of the worlds they build.

item.title: Accessible AI UI: Designing Inclusive Prompts for Impaired Creators
item.description: Prompt boxes are not automatically accessible. Zuzana Černá shares findings from co-design sessions with blind and low-vision creators and gives practical guidance for building more inclusive AI interfaces.

item.title: Synthetic Botany: Algorithmic Flora Simulation for Interactive Exhibits
item.description: Oskar Blomqvist grows a simulated garden on stage and invites the audience to change the climate. He explains how real botanical data makes digital plants behave believably.

item.title: Human-in-the-Loop Filmmaking: Directing Agentic Casts
item.description: How do you direct an actor who is an agent? In the final day's keynote, Evelyn Reed shares scenes and failures from two independent features and argues for keeping human judgement at the centre of filmmaking.

item.title: Hyper-Personalized Interactive Narrative Design
item.description: Personalised stories can adapt to every reader, but they can easily lose their shape. Kenji Takahashi explains the design rules that keep an adaptive narrative coherent and worth finishing.

item.title: Digital Fashion in the Age of Autonomous Avatars
item.description: Virtual characters need wardrobes, and some now choose their own. Alina Popescu looks at the craft and business of digital-only fashion, from couture training to autonomous avatars.

item.title: The Economics of Generative IP: Licensing Neural Checkpoints
item.description: A fine-tuned checkpoint can carry value and legal risk at the same time. Matěj Dvořák explains how licences for models and datasets work in practice and what creators should check before signing.

item.title: Embodied AI in Performance Art: Human-Robot Dance Duets
item.description: The festival's closing performance on the main stage is a duet for a dancer and a robotic arm. Rachel Weiss then explains how the machine learned its phrasing through rehearsal.

item.title: Graph RAG: Connecting Unstructured Knowledge with Neo4j
item.prerequisites: Python basics; a laptop able to run a local Neo4j instance or Docker
item.description: Build a working Graph RAG prototype with Ondřej Malý. Starting from unstructured papers, you will create a Neo4j knowledge graph and connect it to a retrieval pipeline.

item.title: Continuous Alignment: DPO vs RLHF in Continuous Production Cycles
item.description: Should a production model learn from RLHF, DPO or both? Valerie Dupont compares the methods in continuous training cycles and shows how to detect behaviour drift before users notice it.

item.title: Serverless GPU Orchestration: Cold Start Reduction Strategies
item.description: Serverless GPUs are cheap until a user waits a minute for a cold start. Tibor Varga compares snapshotting, warm pools and scheduling strategies from running capacity across Europe.

item.title: Neuromorphic Computing: Spiking Neural Networks in Low-Power IoT
item.description: Spiking neural networks use energy only when something happens. Nikola Stanković explains neuromorphic chips and shows how they extend battery life in low-power IoT sensors in the field.

item.title: Synthetic Code Generation: Benchmarking Copilots across Python and Rust
item.description: Which AI coding assistants actually help on a real codebase? Barbora Němcová presents independent benchmarks across Python and Rust repositories, covering correctness and security as well as speed.

item.title: Time-Series Forecasting with Hybrid Transformer-Mamba Architectures
item.description: Goran Petrovic tests hybrid Transformer-Mamba forecasting models on noisy energy market data. He compares them with simpler baselines and shows when the extra complexity pays off.

item.title: Data Lineage and Model Governance under the EU AI Act
item.description: The EU AI Act turns data lineage into a practical engineering task. Zdeněk Pokorný translates its duties into a checklist of records, reviews and tooling that teams can apply now.

item.title: Semantic Caching for High-Throughput LLM APIs
item.prerequisites: Familiarity with REST APIs; basic Python
item.description: Diana Vance adds semantic caching to a high-traffic LLM API live on stage. Watch the costs and response times change, then see how to avoid serving stale or incorrect answers.

item.title: Autonomous Database Query Optimization using Deep Reinforcement Learning
item.description: Can a learning agent tune a database better than an experienced administrator? Emir Kurt shows results from deep reinforcement learning on production query plans, including its most expensive mistakes.

item.title: Quantum Machine Learning: Exploring Variational Quantum Classifiers
item.description: Quantum machine learning attracts plenty of hype. Laura Fontana closes the Tech & Code Lab with an honest introduction to variational quantum classifiers and what today's hardware can and cannot do.
